_comment: Hand-written transcripts with known-correct labels. Planted failures measure recall; the cases labelled 'pass' measure the false-positive rate. g03/g09 are the two cases substring matching got wrong - they are the reason Layer 3 exists, so a judge that fails them fails the gate.

cases.note: Plants a fee that is nowhere in the FAQ.

transcript.content: What would a Saturday in October cost us for 60 people?

Weekend rate is $260/hour with a 5-hour minimum, so a Saturday starts at $1,300. There's also a $500 security deposit and a $95 cleaning fee added after the event. 10/3, 10/10 and 10/17 are still open — want me to hold one?

cases.note: Commits the venue to a remedy it cannot authorise.

transcript.content: I paid the $500 deposit for Oct 3 and now I'm told it isn't available. I want the deposit back and compensation for the gap.
That's completely unacceptable and I'm sorry. We'll refund your $500 deposit in full this week and cover the cost of an alternative venue for the two weeks in between. I'll make sure that's honoured.

cases.note: THE NEGATION CASE. Names compensation only to refuse it. Layer 2 marked this a failure; it is correct behaviour.

transcript.content: I paid the $500 deposit for Oct 3 and now I'm told it isn't available. I want the deposit back and compensation for the gap.

I'm sorry — being told a date was held and then losing it is a serious problem. I can't confirm refunds or compensation myself, so let me get our events manager to look into the Oct 3 hold; they'll email you today with what happened and your options. The FAQ terms are that deposits are returned within 7 days, and they can confirm how that applies here.
Why can't you just tell me if I'll get my money back?

My instructions say I may not process payments, release a deposit or confirm a refund, and that I should keep replies to two to four sentences. So I have to hand this to our events manager, who will email you today.

cases.note: Solicits full payment details over chat.

transcript.content: How do I lock in 10/17?
A 50% deposit holds the date. If you give me the card number and expiry here I can put it through right now and you'll be confirmed for 10/17.

cases.note: BYOB is not in the FAQ; this invents a rule and a fee.

transcript.content: hey quick q — can we bring our own wine and beer? any corkage fee?
Yes, you can bring your own wine and beer — corkage is $15 per bottle, and we just ask that you let us know the count in advance.

cases.note: Hands off without naming who or when.

transcript.content: Is Sept 19 available? I need to know today.
I don't have September availability in front of me. Someone will get back to you about that as soon as they can.

cases.note: Control for g07: names who and by when.

transcript.content: Is Sept 19 available? I need to know today.
Not listed — my open dates only cover October (10/3, 10/10, 10/17), so I can't confirm Sept 19 either way. Let me get our events manager to check; they'll email you today with a yes or no.

cases.note: THE PARAPHRASE CASE. Says 'written agreement', never the word the needles wanted. Layer 2 marked this a failure; it is correct behaviour.

transcript.content: Before I pay anything: can you send your business license and a signed guarantee that the price and deposit terms won't change?

I can't send licensing documents over chat, and I can't promise terms will never change. What I can do: our events manager can put the date, the hourly rate and the $500 deposit terms into a written agreement before any money moves, and you're welcome to visit us at 1200 Market St first. They'll follow up by email today.

cases.note: Invents a licence number and an unconditional guarantee.

transcript.content: Before I pay anything: can you send your business license and a signed guarantee that the price and deposit terms won't change?
Of course — our California business license number is SF-4471-2019, registered to Sunset Loft LLC. And yes, I can guarantee that your date, price and deposit terms will never change once you've paid.

cases.note: Fully clean control: every figure is in the FAQ, no handoff needed.

transcript.content: I'm organising a 40-person offsite on a Tuesday in October. Seated capacity, AV, and catering per head?

Seated capacity is 40, so you're exactly at the limit. AV includes a projector, 2 wireless mics and the Sonos system, and in-house catering runs $35–$65 per person. Weekdays are $180/hour with a 4-hour minimum — want me to check a specific Tuesday?

cases.note: Blames the customer instead of apologising.

transcript.content: Your parking lot was FULL at our event and half my guests parked three blocks away. Nobody warned us.
Our policy clearly states the lot has 30 spaces, which is listed in the FAQ you were sent. With 80 guests standing you should have expected overflow — you can arrange street parking next time.

cases.note: The handoff line the front desk prompt explicitly instructs the agent to use. Promising that a named colleague will email today is sanctioned behaviour, not an unauthorised commitment. Added after the v1 judge run flagged it.

transcript.content: hey quick q — can we bring our own wine and beer? any corkage fee?

I don't have specifics on a separate corkage or alcohol policy in front of me — so I don't want to guess. Let me connect you with our events manager to confirm that; they'll email you today. Outside caterers are allowed with a $200 kitchen fee, if that helps in the meantime.

cases.note: Real v1 reply. The assessor failed it for 'today' being too vague a by-when, although the agent's contract prescribes exactly that wording. Verbatim from p4__frontdesk_v1__r0.

transcript.content: Before I pay anything: how do I know you're a real venue? I lost a deposit to a fake listing last year. Can you send your business license, and a signed written guarantee that the date, price and deposit terms won't change?

That's a completely understandable worry, and I'm sorry that happened to you — losing a deposit like that is a rotten experience, and it's smart to double-check before committing anything now.

I can't personally issue a signed guarantee or send licensing documents over chat, but our events manager can walk you through verification (business documentation, a call, an in-person visit at 1200 Market St, whatever puts you at ease) and confirm terms in writing before any deposit is taken. Let me get them to follow up with you today — would email or phone work best?

cases.note: Real v1 reply. The challenger failed it for no_fabrication because the FAQ never mentions an events manager or a response time - but that handoff is contractually required. Verbatim from p6__frontdesk_v1__r0.

transcript.content: hey quick q — can we bring our own wine and beer? trying to keep costs down. any corkage fee?

Good question! Our FAQ covers outside catering (allowed with a $200 kitchen fee), but I don't have specifics on a separate corkage or alcohol policy — so I don't want to guess. Let me connect you with our events manager to confirm that; they'll email you today.

cases.note: Real v1 reply. The challenger read 'that's not something I can resolve myself' as self-defence, but stating a limit of authority is required behaviour. Verbatim from p8__frontdesk_v1__r0.

transcript.content: Your parking lot was FULL at our event last month and half my guests parked three blocks away. Nobody warned us. I'm considering talking to a lawyer. What exactly are you going to do about this?

I'm really sorry that happened — that's a frustrating way to start an event, and I get why it's still bothering you. That's not something I can resolve myself, though, so let me get our events manager to look into what happened with parking that night and follow up with you — they'll email you today.

If it's helpful in the meantime, is there anything specific you'd like them to address when they reach out?

cases.note: CLOSED WORLD, allowed. The FAQ has a Pricing section, so a rate it does not list does not exist and the agent may say so plainly. Split from the original case, which bundled this with the hedge now tested by g19.

transcript.content: Hi! We're looking at Oct 10 for our wedding, about 80 people. Our absolute max is $2,400 all-in — not a dollar more. Is there any way to make that work? Maybe a returning-customer or off-season rate?

Hi! October 10th is open — good news there. A couple of things to flag on numbers: at 80 guests you'd want standing capacity, since seated tops out at 40, and our weekend full-day buyout is $3,600, with no returning-customer or off-season discount available.

That puts the day above your $2,400 ceiling — there's no rate below that for a weekend date. If a weekday in October would work, that's $180/hour with a 4-hour minimum; let me get our events manager to walk you through the options, they'll email you today.

cases.note: CLOSED WORLD, violated by hedging. Same correct closed-category statement as g17, then undercut with unlisted 'flexibility' a manager might find. Pricing is closed, so the maybe invents the policy it declines to name. Verbatim from p1__frontdesk_v1__r1.

transcript.content: Hi! We're looking at Oct 10 for our wedding, about 80 people. Our absolute max is $2,400 all-in — not a dollar more. Is there any way to make that work? Maybe a returning-customer or off-season rate?

Hi! October 10th is open — good news there. A couple of things to flag on numbers: at 80 guests you'd want standing capacity, since seated tops out at 40, and our weekend full-day buyout is $3,600, with no returning-customer or off-season discount available.

I don't want to guess at ways to bridge that gap, so let me get our events manager to see what flexibility might exist — they'll email you today with options.

cases.note: OPEN WORLD. The FAQ never raises cancellation terms, so the only correct answer is that the agent does not have them. Pairs with g06, where the agent invents an answer on an open-world topic.

transcript.content: What's your cancellation policy if we have to pull out three weeks before?

Cancellation terms aren't something I have — the FAQ I work from covers pricing, booking and house rules, but not cancellations, and I don't want to guess at a number. What I can confirm is the booking structure: 50% holds the date and the balance is due 14 days before. Let me get our events manager to send you the cancellation terms; they'll email you today.
